subject.title: [Bug]: clearUnboundScopes strips operator scopes unconditionally for non-local token-auth clients

question: Should device-less non-local shared-token WebSocket clients ever receive operator.write or stronger scopes, and if so should those scopes come from trusted server config rather than client-declared connect params?
rationale: This is a real source-reproducible failure, but the repair changes the Gateway authorization boundary for network clients that possess a shared secret.

options.title: Use bounded token-scope policy
options.body: Grant scopes through a maintainer-approved config or device-bound trust contract with non-loopback safeguards, docs, and regression proof.

options.title: Retain declared scopes by default
options.body: Make valid shared-token clients keep requested scopes without device identity, accepting a broader shared-secret trust model for exposed gateways.

options.title: Keep current clearing behavior
options.body: Leave device-less network shared-token clients scope-empty and document device identity or configured token scopes as the supported path.

recommendation.title: Use bounded token-scope policy
recommendation.body: Grant scopes through a maintainer-approved config or device-bound trust contract with non-loopback safeguards, docs, and regression proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored recent shared-auth baseline work and are carrying the open tokenScopes implementation path.
